hook: Think inflation is cooling off? That 3.4 percent official headline rate is a lie when you actually look at your everyday bills.

sections.voiceover: The official story is that annual inflation slowed to 3.4 percent, while core inflation is down to 2.5 percent. But those CPI numbers strip out the real pain. The price of gasoline actually surged by 24.6 percent, driving massive fuel costs.

beats.text: The official annual inflation rate of 3.4 percent is dwarfed by surging fuel costs.

visual.concept: official rates contrasted with soaring fuel costs

beats.text: Headline Consumer Price Index numbers hide the true impact of daily expenses.

b_roll: Gas station pump showing rising price digits
Close up of hands refueling a car

sections.voiceover: And it gets worse at the grocery store. Cumulative grocery prices are 32 percent higher than they were in 2020. This forces average households to spend an extra 1200 to 1400 dollars more every single year.

beats.text: Cumulative grocery prices have surged by 32 percent compared to the baseline year.

visual.concept: grocery prices rising much faster than other categories
visual.primary: giant grocery cart icon next to a standard basket

beats.text: Families must find up to 1400 dollars more per year just to buy the same food.

series.label: Lower bound of additional grocery cost
Upper bound of additional grocery cost

b_roll: Person scanning grocery receipts with a calculator
Overhead view of a conveyor belt filled with groceries

sections.voiceover: This means the classic fifty-thirty-twenty budgeting rule is completely broken. Instead of spending just half on needs, average household spending on basic necessities has skyrocketed. It now swallows 62 percent of average income, leaving almost nothing for savings.

beats.text: Necessities now swallow 62 percent of the average pre-tax household budget.

series.label: Average household spending share on necessities

visual.concept: necessities taking up more than half of income
visual.primary: income bar with a dominant necessities section

beats.text: Traditional budgeting percentages fail to represent current economic reality.

Stressed individual looking at bills on a kitchen counter

sections.voiceover: You must recalculate your actual needs bucket using these real fuel and grocery rates instead of generic advice. Stop relying on outdated formulas from 2020. Adjust your spending limits today, and subscribe to Money Mind for real, proven financial strategies that actually work.
